This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, praying to modify the judgment and award dated 31-01-2020 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT at Kundapura in MVC No.491/2018 to the extent of disallowed claim and allow this appeal by enhancing the compensation, in the interest of justice.

This Miscellaneous First Appeal having been heard through physical hearing/video conferencing hearing and reserved on 13-03-2023, coming on for pronouncement of judgment, this day, the Court delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the petitioners (claimants) under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the M.V. Act"), seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Kundapura, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal', for short), in its judgment and award dated 31-01-2020, in M.V.C.No.491/2018.
2.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Kundapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The summary of the case of the claimants before the Tribunal was that, on the date 15-02-2018, at about 00:15 hours, while the deceased was proceeding on his Motor Cycle bearing registration No.
KA-20/EL-1218 from Jaddinabailu side towards Kundapura side, near Koni High School Cross Road, Koni village, Kundapura Taluk, a Bus bearing registration No.KA-20/C-2824 belonging to the first respondent and being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, coming from Kundapura side towards Siddapura side, dashed to the Motor Cycle of the deceased, due to which road traffic accident, he sustained severe injuries and died on the same day at about 06:10 hours at K.M.C. Hospital, Manipal.

The claimants before the Tribunal contended that, they have spent a sum of `1,00,000/- for treatment, a sum of `25,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies and a sum of `25,000/-
towards conveyance charges.

They further contended that at the time of the road traffic accident, the deceased Bharath Raj Mudaliyar, was aged about 20 years and hale and healthy and was pursuing Dharmaraja vs Sadananda Chathra on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136413938/
2 his II Semester of B.E. course at MITK Engineering College.
The claimants have lost their son's love and affection and support.

Holding that the first respondent as owner and second respondent as the insurer of the offending bus, the claimants have claimed a compensation of a sum of `25,00,000/-
from the respondents with interest thereupon at `12.5% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation.

3. In response to the notice, both the respondents appeared before the Tribunal and filed their statement of objections, wherein both the respondents denied the averments made in the claim petition regarding the manner of occurrence of the road traffic accident and also age of the deceased and the alleged expenditure said to have been met by the claimants.
They specifically denied that there was any rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the alleged offending Bus.

4. Before the Tribunal, the claimants got examined claimant No.1 - the father of the deceased Bharath Raj Mudaliyar as PW-1 and one Sri. Shamith Shetty as PW-2 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-20.

On behalf of the respondents, though no witness was examined, however, a copy of the Insurance Policy was got marked as Ex.R-1.
5.

After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:

The Tribunal awarded compensation of a sum of `20,98,322/- with interest at the rate of `6% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of deposit of the award amount, holding the owner and Insurer jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation and directed the respondent No.2 - Insurer to deposit the award amount.

Aggrieved by the same, contending that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side, the claimants before the Tribunal have filed the present appeal, seeking enhancement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Bharath Raj Mudaliyar in the road traffic accident in question.

3 7.
The second respondent herein - Insurance Company is represented by its learned counsel.
On a memo filed by the learned counsel for the appellants, notice to first respondent (owner of the offending vehicle) is dispensed with.
8. Learned counsel for the appellants (claimants) and learned counsel for the respondent No.2 (Insurer) are physically appearing before the Court.
9. Records were called for from the Tribunal and the same are placed before the Court.
10. Though this appeal is posted at the stage of Admission, however, with the consent from the learned counsels from both side, the same is taken up for its final disposal.
11. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the materials placed before this Court including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the records of the Tribunal.

12. The present appeal being the claimants' appeal and the respondent No.2 (Insurer)
having not preferred either cross-objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of a road traffic accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimants and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is not in dispute.
Furthermore, the claimant No.1 - Sri. Dharmaraja, father of the deceased got himself examined as PW-1, wherein he reiterated the contentions taken up by the claimants in their claim petition.

He also got produced and marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-20, which inter alia includes copies of the FIR, statement of the complainant, scene of offence panchanama, sketch of the scene of offence,
Post-Mortem report, inquest panchanama, AIR report, IMV report, medical bills, marks card of the deceased and charge sheet.
The charge sheet at Ex.P-19 has accused the driver of the offending Bus for the rash and negligent driving and causing the death of the deceased Bharath Raj Mudaliar.
The study certificate and the marks card of the deceased would go to show that the deceased was studying in an Engineering Degree Course as at the time of the road traffic accident.
Thus, it stands established that the accident, as alleged by the claimants, has occurred on the date, time and place and the manner as contended by the claimants in the claim petition.

Thus, the only question that remains for consideration is, whether the claimants are entitled for any enhancement in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on account of the death of the deceased Bharath Raj Mudaliyar in the road traffic accident in question.
13. The learned counsel for the appellants (claimants) in his brief argument submitted that, his only grievance is about the quantification of the compensation towards loss of dependency.

He submitted that even though the deceased was a bachelor, however, in the rural areas like the place where the Dharmaraja vs Sadananda Chathra on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136413938/
4 deceased was living, even the students also earn for their family, by working in the family business.

As such, the income of the deceased is liable to be taken on the higher side and the deduction towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased should have been taken at 1/3rd instead of 50% of the assessed income.
In his support, the learned counsel for the appellants relied upon two judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court, which would be referred to at an appropriate stage hereafterwards.

14. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 (Insurance Company) in her brief argument submitted that, since admittedly, the deceased was a bachelor, the claimants being the parents of the - 10 - deceased, the Tribunal has rightly deducted 50% of the assessed income of the deceased towards his personal and living expenses, which does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.

15. Regarding the quantum of compensation, the Post-Mortem report at Ex.P-5, inquest panchanama at Ex.P-6 and the other police documents showing the age of the deceased Bharath Raj Mudaliyar as 20 years, has not been denied or disputed from either side.
As such, the age of the deceased is required to be taken as 20 years, for which age, the proper multiplier applicable is '18'.

The contention of the claimants that the deceased was studying in II Semester of B.E. course in Computer Science at MITK Engineering College, Moodlakatte, is corroborated by the documentary evidence such as the Study Certificate at Ex.P-15 and the marks card at Ex.P-16.
The marks card at Ex.P-16 shows that the deceased has passed the I semester of B.E. (Computer Science) with good marks.

Though the learned counsel for the appellants contended that the deceased, apart from - 11 - pursuing his studies was also assisting his parents in the domestic work, however, there is no evidence in that regard.
Still, the bright prospects which the deceased Bharath Raj Mudaliyar had as a bright student of Engineering in Computer Science Branch cannot be ignored.

Therefore, though normally large number of Motor Accident Claims Tribunals would take, in the absence of any proof of income, a notional income at a sum of `12,500/- per month for the relevant year 2018, in which year, the road traffic accident in question has occurred, however, I am of the view that considering the special facts and circumstances of the case and confining to the present case only, the notional income of the deceased would be appropriate if it is taken at a sum of `15,000/- per month.

As per the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, considering the deceased as self- employed person, for his age group, the future prospects - 12 - Dharmaraja vs Sadananda Chathra on 20 March, 2023

5 at 40% of his income is required to be taken.
Thus, a sum of `6,000/- (40% of `15,000/-) is to be added to the monthly income of the deceased at `15,000/- which comes to `21,000/- per month.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarala Verma (Smt.) and others Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, the deceased being a bachelor, 50% of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

which reads as below:
- 13 - 5.

sentences.text: The first respondent appealed against the judgment of MACT before the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam.

entities.text: High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The High Court, vide its impugned judgment, reduced the compensation to `85,000/-
along with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.

the relevant portion of the High Court judgment reads as follows:
"Heard both sides.

The learned Government Pleader submits that father was aged about 70 years even at the time of the accident and therefore the Tribunal had committed an error in fixing the multiplier at 16 whereas it has to only apply a multiplier of 5.

In the award, the age of the first claimant is not shown but the daughter of the first claimant, namely, Leela has filed an affidavit before this Court for getting impleaded as IA No.1407 of 2006 where her age is shown as 61 years.
So it is clear that she would be 49 years at the time of the accident and therefore even if the minimum age that can be fixed for the mother will be 67 years and not less.
The mother is the real legal representative and others cannot claim the status of legal representative and therefore the appropriate multiplier to be used in this case is only 5.
It is true that the Tribunal has taken his income at `1200 per month whereas the claimants claimed that the deceased was getting an amount of `1500 as his income.
We fix it at - 14 - `1500, deduct 1/3rd for personal expenses and applying a multiplier of 5 the loss of dependency compensation would come to `60,000.
The Tribunal has awarded `15,000 towards pain and suffering, `1,000 towards transportation charges and `2000 for funeral expenses.
They are only just and reasonable and we do not find any ground to interfere with the same.
But the Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards love and affection.

Hence, we grant an amount of `5000 under that Dharmaraja vs Sadananda Chathra on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136413938/
6 head and also award a sum of `2500 towards loss of estate.
Therefore, the total compensation that the claimants are entitled to will be `85,000.""

In the light of the above observation, the learned counsel submitted that in the instant case also, the deduction towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased should have been confined to 1/3rd of the income of the deceased.

The said argument of the learned counsel for the appellants is not acceptable for the reason that, in P.S.Somanathan's case (supra), admittedly, the age of the deceased was 33 years and he had more number of dependents than two upon him.
A reference about his - 15 - father - the first claimant and daughter of the first claimant are made in the extracted paragraph No.5 above.

Thus, there being three or more number of dependents upon the deceased, the deduction towards the personal expenses of the deceased was confined to 1/3rd of the income of the deceased, whereas in the instant case, the dependents/claimants are only two in number who are parents of the deceased Bharath Raj Mudaliyar, who was a bachelor.
Therefore, there is no reason to take the deduction towards the personal expenses at 1/3rd of the income of the deceased from  which has been taken by the Tribunal.

Secondly, he relied upon another judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Gopali and Ors reported in AIR 2012 SUPREME COURT 3381, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court in an appeal before it with respect to Section 168 of the M.V. Act was pleased to observe that the deduction towards the personal expenses at some percentage was standardised because of the difficulty for the respondents in a claim - 16 - petition to produce the evidence to show that the deceased was spending a considerable part of his income on himself or that he was contributing only a small part of the income towards his family.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Gopali and Ors reported in AIR 2012 SUPREME COURT 3381
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court further observed in paragraph 14 of its judgment that, the practice of standardising and deducting towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased as 1/3rd of the income, if the deceased was married and  (50%) of the income, if the deceased was a bachelor, was evolved with experience, logic and convenience.
But such percentage of deduction is not an inflexible rule and offers merely a guideline.

In the instant case, since the deceased was a student aged about 20 years, and the claimants are only two in number, who are his parents, I do not find any reason to reduce the deduction towards the personal expenses of the deceased from 50% to Dharmaraja vs Sadananda Chathra on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136413938/
7 1/3rd.
As such, the argument of the learned counsel for the appellants on the said point is not acceptable.

- 17 - Thus the compensation towards loss of dependency for which the appellants/claimants should be entitled to would be the contribution of the deceased towards his family (claimants), i.e. `21,000/- (-) 50% (i.e. `10,500/-) = `10,500/-,
which is the income of the deceased per month.
As analysed above, the multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased is '18'.
Thus, the quantum of compensation towards loss of dependency would be a sum of `10,500/-x12x'18' =`22,68,000/-.
Since the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `18,14,400/- under the said head, the parents are entitled for a differential amount of a sum of `4,53,600/- as the enhancement.

16. Since the claimants are the parents of the deceased, the Tribunal, by relying upon a judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM @ CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS) reported in 2018 SCC OnLine SC 1546, has awarded a sum of `40,000/-x2 = `80,000/- towards filial consortium, which is just and proper and does not call for interference at the hands of this Court.

sentences.text:
Towards loss of love and affection to both the claimants, the Tribunal has found it necessary to award some compensation though the compensation towards loss of filial consortium was awarded,
as such, it has awarded a sum of `1,00,000/- under the said head of loss of filial love and affection.
The same being reasonable, does not call for interference at the hands of this Court.

18. Towards the heads of loss of estate and funeral, obsequies expenses and transportation of dead body, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `15,000/- + `15,000/-, respectively as compensation,
which does not warrant any interference by this Court.

19. Towards the medical expenses, based upon the medical bills produced and marked as per Exs.P-9 to P-14, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `73,922/-, as such, the compensation awarded under this head also does not warrant any interference or modification at the hands of this Court.
- 19 - Thus, in total, the claimants are entitled for an additional compensation only for the differential amount under the head of loss of dependency which a sum of `4,53,600/-.

It is to that extent only,
the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal warrants interference at the hands of this Court.

Barring the above, the claimants are not entitled for compensation under any other head or enhancement or modification of compensation under the existing heads.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER [i] The appeal filed by the claimants stands allowed in part;
[ii] The impugned judgment and award dated 31-01-2020, passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., at Kundapura, in M.V.C.No.491/2018,
awarding a total compensation of `20,98,322/- to the petitioners (appellants herein)
is modified and - 20 - enhanced by a sum of `4,53,600/-, thus, bringing the total entitlement of compensation by the appellants/petitioners to a sum of `25,51,922/- with `6% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of deposit.
[iii] Rest of the terms of the order of the Tribunal including fixing of liability upon the respondents, more particularly, upon the second respondent- Insurance Company,
rate of interest, ratio of apportionment of the compensation, deposit and its release,
etc. remains unaltered.
Draw modified award accordingly.

18. Towards the heads of loss of estate and funeral, obsequies expenses and transportation of dead body, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `15,000/- + `15,000/-, respectively as compensation,
which does not warrant any interference by this Court.
19. Towards the medical expenses, based upon the medical bills produced and marked as per Exs.P-9 to P-14, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `73,922/-, as such, the compensation awarded under this head also does not warrant any interference or modification at the hands of this Court.
- 19 - Thus, in total, the claimants are entitled for an additional compensation only for the differential amount under the head of loss of dependency which a sum of `4,53,600/-.
It is to that extent only,
the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal warrants interference at the hands of this Court.
Barring the above, the claimants are not entitled for compensation under any other head or enhancement or modification of compensation under the existing heads.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER [i] The appeal filed by the claimants stands allowed in part;
[ii] The impugned judgment and award dated 31-01-2020, passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., at Kundapura, in M.V.C.No.491/2018,
awarding a total compensation of `20,98,322/- to the petitioners (appellants herein)
is modified and - 20 - enhanced by a sum of `4,53,600/-, thus, bringing the total entitlement of compensation by the appellants/petitioners to a sum of `25,51,922/- with `6% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of deposit.
[iii] Rest of the terms of the order of the Tribunal including fixing of liability upon the respondents, more particularly, upon the second respondent- Insurance Company,
rate of interest, ratio of apportionment of the compensation, deposit and its release,
etc. remains unaltered.
Draw modified award accordingly.
The Registry to transmit a copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal, along with its records, immediately.
